thread.title: Apple: Hope for an 'iTV' Springs Eternal

title: Apple: Hope for an 'iTV' Springs Eternal
text:
David Marino-Nachison May 4, 2018 12:57 p.m. ET
Some dreams never die—like the dream of a New Order reunion , or Chipotle breakfast . Or, say, an Apple TV.
No, not that Apple TV . We mean a television set, made by Apple (AAPL). Newsletter Sign-up
For some folks, the idea is at the top of their “Why isn’t there a…” lists. (Here’s one fan’s “ concept trailer ,” from 2015.) Rumors of an “iTV” have surfaced, and then been squashed, to varying degrees, for years. Lately, things have been quiet, as they have been since last summer when some blurry, inconclusive images circulated on a Chinese website.
On the latest quarterly conference call, there was nary a mention . (Rather read about iPhone sales? Here’s Tiernan Ray’s take from Thursday .)
But on Friday, RBC Capital Management raised the subject again. In a note detailing their support of the Barron’s Next 50 company—they have an “outperform” rating and a $203 price target, about 11% above current levels on the stock—the analysts said an iTV might help the business over time.
“We believe new products (such as an iTV) could further expand Apple’s revenue opportunity and profit potential,” they wrote. (Other parts of their thesis included growth in emerging markets and enterprise business.) “Apple’s current stock price creates an attractive entry point for investors,” the analysts wrote.
CEO Tim Cook has complained about television, generally—notably in 2014, when he said during a television interview: “Think how much your life has changed, and all the things around you that have changed, and yet TV, when you go into the living room to watch TV or wherever it may be, it almost feels like you’re rewinding the clock.”
But if a television set is coming, it’s been kept mighty quiet. Apple has launched other new products, such as the HomePod smart speaker , and its designs on video content have been widely reported. CNET recently reported on an in-development virtual/augmented reality headset that could debut in 2020.
The company, of course, could just be keeping mum. Apple didn’t respond to an question about iTV emailed to an account for media on Friday morning. In the absence of an outright denial, hope springs eternal.
